identity.title: On Path to Multimodal Generalist: General-Level and General-Bench

problem.claim: Assess whether higher performance across multimodal tasks adequately indicates stronger generalist capability and progress toward human-level AI.

gap.claim: The abstract argues that task performance alone does not straightforwardly characterize multimodal generalist capability.

contributions.claim: Introduces General-Level, a five-scale framework for assessing MLLM performance and generality using synergy across comprehension, generation, and multimodal interactions.
Presents General-Bench, covering over 700 tasks and 325,800 instances across a broad range of skills, modalities, formats, and capabilities.
Reports an evaluation of over 100 existing state-of-the-art MLLMs that identifies capability rankings and highlights challenges in reaching genuine AI.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their project by combining a five-scale generality framework centered on synergy with a broad multimodal benchmark for evaluating generalists.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report rankings of over 100 existing state-of-the-art MLLMs and describe persistent challenges in reaching genuine AI.
The authors report that General-Bench contains over 700 tasks and 325,800 instances spanning diverse skills, modalities, formats, and capabilities.

narrative_sequence.summary: MLLMs are moving from specialist systems toward multimodal generalists that understand and generate across increasingly fine-grained and diverse modalities.
The growth of benchmark test sets raises whether higher cross-task performance is sufficient evidence of stronger generalist capability; the authors argue the answer is not straightforward.
The project introduces General-Level, a five-scale assessment of MLLM performance and generality, with synergy as the central criterion.
General-Bench broadens evaluation coverage, and results involving more than 100 state-of-the-art MLLMs reveal capability rankings and challenges toward genuine AI.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates raw task performance from generality and evaluates whether synergy is preserved across comprehension, generation, and multimodal interactions.

lessons.interpretation: This suggests that broad capability claims benefit from an explicit behavioral criterion, not only aggregate scores.
lessons.application: Define a cross-capability criterion and test it alongside per-task performance when presenting a generalist evaluation.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the target system supports only one modality or one capability family.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five level definitions, synergy measurements, aggregation procedure, or ranking values.
It does not report baseline comparisons, statistical uncertainty, or independent validation of the framework and benchmark.
